After several consecutive weeks of only weekly usage caps, OpenAI today announced that it will restore the five-hour usage limit for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work. Details below.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers' five-hour usage cap restored

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, head of Codex and ChatGPT engineering at OpenAI, announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), Plus subscribers will see the five-hour usage limit restored on Codex and ChatGPT Work.

Once users hit either the five-hour or weekly usage cap, they can wait for the next cycle to reset, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also occasionally reset users' usage caps for free, while stored reset credits can be earned through specific promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI had temporarily lifted the five-hour limits on Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly caps in place.

During this period, the company also repeatedly reset users' weekly allowances ahead of schedule to celebrate milestones, including reaching an additional one million active users across the two (now merged) platforms.

However, as Tibo explained on X tonight:

Tomorrow we will restore the five-hour limits for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex. I mentioned this before but then postponed it. This is necessary because (1) the five-hour limit helps us spread out compute load so that we can maintain a more generous plan on the weekly side; (2) the majority of users on the Plus plan are more casual and newer users, who often accidentally burn through the entire week's allowance and then feel confused, resulting in a poor experience. Over the coming months, we will not be enabling five-hour limits on $100 and $200 Pro subscriptions.

Tibo made no mention of any changes to Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently operate on a separate credit-based usage system.

Does the restoration of five-hour limits on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
